searchText: I think you are referring to <@686695036733227017>, but I believe the difficulty bomb block time increments should not affect the merge time since the difficulty per block will increase along with the block time increments... If you are looking to take Ethereum offline, this is one of the rare opportunities where it is possible. Not sure if this classifies as a "troll" or not, but it is pretty significant. While theoretically it is possible, technically it is not. Doubling hashrate of the largest GPU PoW coin is impossible. why double when you can eclipse attack as well ? how much of a network partition would be necessary to make it technically possible or is that not relevant yup not relevant First, this kind of attacks is easily detectable, second, you don’t have access to other people’s mining rigs 💯 what I thought after https://eth2docs.vercel.app Exactly as the other Mario explained (thanks <@892053833121923094>! 🙂 ) , bomb raises difficulty per block which decreases block time but difficulty over time stays roughly the same. Details on estimating mainnet TTD are in this write up https://notes.ethereum.org/@MarioHavel/merge-ttd Regarding rolling estimates which are updated at Bordel.wtf, it does polynomial regression and updates every few hours so it always recalculates estimation based on latest difficulty growth trend Thanks both for the explenation 🙂 Even if you could add 800 TH/s to eth, probably a lot of miners will stop mining because the difficulty will skyrocket 💯 You're saying they're rational and just want to make money? They're not interested in trolling Ethereum if it's on their pocketbook? What did I buy this 🍿 maker for?!? The new game of thrones series?? *among other things, including every crypto user asking "which government is doing this?"

excerpts.content:
Exactly as the other Mario explained (thanks <@892053833121923094>! 🙂 ) , bomb raises difficulty per block which decreases block time but difficulty over time stays roughly the same. Details on estimating mainnet TTD are in this write up https://notes.ethereum.org/@MarioHavel/merge-ttd
Regarding rolling estimates which are updated at Bordel.wtf, it does polynomial regression and updates every few hours so it always recalculates estimation based on latest difficulty growth trend
